newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats lash Britain, US on assembly climbdown.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats lash Britain, US on assembly climbdown.

text.p: Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp lambasted Britain and the United States on Thursday for caving in and sending officials to the swearing-in of a new legislature shortly after the territory reverts to China next week.

Both countries had earlier said they would not attend the investiture of the Beijing-appointed provisional legislature, which China will put in place of Hong Kong's elected chamber upon the sovereignty changeover at midnight June 30.
But Britain backtracked on Wednesday, saying it would send two senior diplomats to the new chamber's investiture, after the United States made a similar move to send its Hong Kong envoy.
Prominent pro-democracy fighters in Hong Kong gave London and Washington a tongue lashing.
"I think they are very disgusting and contemptible. But I am not surprised," said legislator Emily Lau, a voice of democracy in the territory.
"I think people expect the British and Amercian governments to be very weak. If they do this, they just invite contempt.
"They say one thing but refuse to back it up with action ... it is a question of consistency, of being responsible for your public statements," Lau told local radio.
Even some moderate politicians were startled.
"It is baffling to see them blowing, as it were, hot and cold," said Ronald Arculli, a legislator with the usually pro-China Liberal Party.

Beijing plans to have the new chamber sworn in shortly after the midnight handover party, to secure international recognition for a body which pro-democracy nations particularly in the West had been condemning.
